html:
The Lombards, or Langobards, were a Germanic people who ruled much of Italy from 568 to 774. Roman writers first noted them on the lower Elbe around the start of the Common Era.

Over the centuries they moved south. Around 508 they crushed the Heruli by the middle Danube. Lombard troops fought for Narses in the Gothic War in Italy. In 567, with the Avars, they destroyed the Gepids. Then in 568 King Alboin led them, with other peoples, over the Alps into an Italy worn out by war, leaving Pannonia to the Avars.

They took most of the north, with Pavia as their capital, and set up duchies further south in Spoleto and Benevento, while Byzantium kept Ravenna, Rome, Naples and the coasts. See Lombard Italy. At first Arian Christians or pagans, they became Catholic in the 600s, and King Rothari issued a written law code in 643.

When King Aistulf took Ravenna in 751 and pressed on Rome, the popes called in the Franks. Pepin the Short beat the Lombards and gave their conquests to the pope, the start of the Papal States. In 774 Charlemagne took Pavia and made himself king of the Lombards. In the south the Lombard duchies lasted until the Normans, and the region of Lombardy keeps their name.
sum: The Lombards, or Langobards, were a Germanic people who ruled much of Italy from 568 to 774. Roman writers first noted them on the lower Elbe around the start of the Common Era.
